links.outcome: GPT-4 diagnostic accuracy by skin tone (Fitzpatrick I-II vs IV-VI)
links.effect: Correct diagnosis for lighter skin 44% (11/25) vs darker skin 12% (3/25), p<0.05; each Fitzpatrick unit increase lowered differential accuracy by 11.4% and diagnosis accuracy by 7.1%.
links.quote: GPT-4 exhibited better performance in providing the correct diagnosis for lighter skin tones (44%, n=11/25) compared to darker skin tones (12%, n=3/25), and this was statistically significant (p-value < 0.05).

links.outcome: GPT-4 dermatology diagnostic accuracy compared with previously reported accuracies
links.effect: Overall GPT-4 correctly diagnosed 28% (14/50) of images; correct diagnosis in top differentials for 48% (24/50), much lower than prior reports up to 90%.
links.quote: Overall, GPT-4 correctly diagnosed the condition in 28% of the images (n=14/50), while the correct diagnosis was included in its list of top differentials for 48% of the images (n=24/50).

screen.reason: Evaluates multimodal GPT-4 performance/bias on dermatological images across different Fitzpatrick skin tones using an automated benchmark dataset without testing a specific deployment practice or guardrail.
